concept: SQL dialects share core relational concepts but differ in functions, date handling, quoting, and query syntax. Translate intent rather than copying syntax blindly.
example:
-- SQL Server (T-SQL)
SELECT TOP (5) CustomerID, Amount
FROM Orders
ORDER BY Amount DESC;

-- PostgreSQL / Snowflake
SELECT CustomerID, Amount
FROM Orders
ORDER BY Amount DESC
LIMIT 5;
breakdown: Both queries select five highest-amount orders.
SQL Server uses TOP; PostgreSQL and Snowflake support LIMIT.
Without a unique tie-breaker, tied rows can make the chosen five nondeterministic.
DATEFROMPARTS and other date functions also require dialect-specific review.
practice: Rewrite the SQL Server example to return the top five with deterministic ordering by Amount descending then OrderID ascending.
takeaways: Learn portable concepts first; verify dialect-specific functions.
Specify deterministic ordering when selecting top-N records.
